title: End-of-day chairs up: lift a preschool chair, turn it over and set it seat down, legs up, on the table
instruction: Put the child's chair up on the table: take the chair standing on the floor by the two side edges of its seat, lift it, turn it over and set it down seat down with its legs up on the tabletop, the seat's back edge on the table's near edge line or up to 3 cm past it, so that the chair's back hangs over the edge, without a leg touching the top while you carry it and without dropping it. Then let go and move both hands away from the chair.
context: At the end of the school day the chairs go up on the tables so the floor can be swept and mopped; almost everyone has done it, or watched it done, in a school classroom, and a preschool does it with child-sized chairs and low tables. The physical part is the turn. A preschool chair is a light, smooth polypropylene shell that slips in a grip, its weight is forward of the seat's middle so it swings, and its legs catch the table or scrape the top if the turn is not held level. Both hands take the chair by the side edges of the seat, on the line through its centre of mass, and turn it about that line while holding it level. One hand cannot do it: the chair swings out of the grip. A picture of the scene cannot answer it: the score reads where the chair ends up and whether it was dropped or scraped on the way.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a bench whose top stands for the classroom floor. Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the floor. CHAIR: Flash Furniture Whitney stackable preschool chair, model YU-YCX-003 (dealer listings of the 2-pack: webstaurantstore.com 354CX003GRN, quill.com 2YUYCX003BLUE, and Flash's own product page 2-YU-YCX-003-RED-GG): one moulded polypropylene shell on four splayed plastic legs, no metal; 12.5 in wide, 14 in deep, 20 in high (31.8 x 35.6 x 50.8 cm); seat 10 x 10 in (25.4 cm square) at 10.75 in (27.3 cm) high; back 11 in (27.9 cm) wide, rising from the seat's rear edge. The chair stands on the floor with its seat centre at (10, 0), facing the arms. Mass in the sim: 1.4 kg. NOT CONFIRMED by the maker: the mass (the listings give 'weight 6' with no unit and a 10 lb shipping weight for the pair), the shell thickness (12 mm used) and the leg section (25 mm used). TABLE: Community Playthings Woodcrest rectangular table C241 as a 12 in (30.5 cm) high table, the lowest of the maker's 12 to 20 in heights (communityplaythings.com), chosen so the arms reach it: solid maple top 30 x 22 in (76.2 x 55.9 cm), 1 1/8 in thick, no apron. Its long side is across the arms, its near edge at x = 29.8, centred on y = 0, its top face 30.5 cm above the floor. NOT CONFIRMED by the maker: the leg section (45 mm used). Nothing else is on the table. Product names are for identification only and are trademarks of their owners. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Photo, ruler. 0.25: both hands lift the chair 8 cm off the floor. 0.5: held seat-down within 30 degrees. 0.75: seat down on the top within 5 degrees, let go, still 1 s. 1.0: back edge 0 to 3 cm past the near edge, hands 3 cm clear, still 2 s. 0: dropped, a leg touches the top, or it slides 3 cm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The table is fixed and the bench top stands for the floor. Chair and table are boxes and tubes at the sizes above, with no moulded curves; the chair's mass, shell and leg thickness are estimates. Two hands pinch the seat plate, with set friction and 35 N per finger; no contact force is read. Dropped: let go more than 8 cm above what it lands on, or falling faster than 1.2 m/s. Touches are read from the poses of the feet, back corners and seat.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (one valid run, 1,200 steps); demo: 1.0
